title: National Medical Commission bans doctors & hospitals from using AI-generated patient testimonials, fake cu
source_used: The Economic Times (short text) plus Deccan Chronicle for details
key_facts: India's National Medical Commission (NMC) has barred doctors and hospitals from using AI to create fake patient testimonials, fabricated treatment outcomes and endorsements.
The guidelines on ethical advertising and public communication came into force with immediate effect, issued 'earlier this week' per Deccan Chronicle.
They also ban deepfake images and synthetic voices to promote services, buying or manipulating reviews and ratings, and paying to manipulate search rankings.
Claims such as 'guaranteed cure' or 'miracle treatment' need an objectively verifiable basis.
Penalties are graded: warning and ethics training first, censure and a monetary penalty second, suspension of registration for three to six months for a third violation.
Doctors may still share accurate factual medical information and public health material.
quote_evidence: The NMC has barred doctors and hospitals from using AI to create fake patient testimonials or clinical outcomes, and from paying to manipulate search engine and app rankings.
A third violation may lead to suspension of medical registration for three to six months.
why_it_matters_hint: Sets penalties for AI-faked medical advertising in India.
event_date: Guidelines issued 'earlier this week' (exact day not stated); reported 8 Oct 2026
notes: ET text is a short paywalled synopsis; penalty and scope details come from Deccan Chronicle. NMC document not seen. Exact issue date unclear, so not marked stale.
